evidence: This policy statement sets out the final rules and guidance on operational resilience and the management of third-party technology risk for firms authorised by the Financial Services Oversight Authority.
Disruption to financial services can cause serious harm to consumers and to market integrity.
Our objective is that firms can continue to deliver their most important services through severe but plausible disruption
We expect firms to treat operational resilience as a matter for the board, not only for technology teams.
This policy statement takes effect on 1 January 2027.
The deadlines for individual requirements are set out in the relevant sections, and transitional arrangements for some firms are set out in section 9.

evidence: An important business service is a service that a firm provides to an external end user, where disruption to the service could cause intolerable harm to consumers

evidence: An impact tolerance is the maximum tolerable level of disruption to an important business service, expressed as a maximum length of time
A material third-party provider is a provider of technology services whose failure would cause the firm to breach an impact tolerance for one or more important business services.
major incident is an operational incident that has caused, or is likely to cause, a breach of an impact tolerance, or that affects more than 10% of the firm's customers.
Business days are days other than weekends and public holidays in our jurisdiction.
